description: ODC: the answer to 'mandatory event without a handler: refusal or warning?' in the ODC lane, and the answer is the SAME as in O11 - neither refusal nor warning: the kernel applies everything without saying anything (ok=True) and Verify gives ERROR EventHandlerRequiredAction, leaving the module invalid. The block WfPingPanel declares OnPing with IsMandatory true and two instances are born on the screen WfPingDemo without a handler: TWO errors come out, one per instance, each on the path of its IEventHandler - the requirement is charged per INSTANCE, not per block. The same O11 detail also holds: the IEventHandler is born with the instance even when empty, so the two instances without a handler already count as consumers in the `usages`. Parity confirmed with tests/jobs/block-events-mandatory-reactive.json; the valid path (the same IsMandatory true, one handler per instance) is in tests/jobs-odc/block-events-two-instances.json.

expectedMessages.why: THIS is the result that the job exists to prove in the ODC lane: with IsMandatory true, the instance without a handler produces an error (not a warning) on its own IEventHandler. Silencing this would be erasing the proof.
The second message proves that the charge is per INSTANCE and not per block or per event: two instances without a handler give two errors, with different paths.
